facts.text: itomori/Navigation2DEnv-v0 is registered with entry point itomori.envs:Navigation2DEnv and max_episode_steps=300
The constructor defaults render_mode to 'human' and accepts only 'human' or 'rgb_array'
The constructor's default map_filepath is the relative path itomori/navigation2d_config/maps/10x10/10x10_NoObstacle.json

default_uav_args sets velocity_initial 0, velocity_min 0, velocity_max 50, velocity_change_min -10, velocity_change_max 100, angle_initial 0, angle_change_min -10, angle_change_max 10, delta_T 0.1, gps_uncertainty_initial 0.5 and gps_uncertainty_increment 0.02
load_uav_args documents velocity in m/s, angle change in degrees/s, velocity change in m/s**2, delta_T in s and GPS uncertainty in m

The observation space is a Dict of origin (x, y in 0..50), destination (x, y in 0..size) and agent_location (x, y in 0..size; velocity in velocity_min..velocity_max; angle unbounded and risk/GPS uncertainty in 0..inf)
The action space is a Box(2) of [angle change, velocity change] with low [angle_change_min, velocity_change_min] and high [angle_change_max, velocity_change_max], dtype float
The starting agent location is [origin x, origin y, velocity_initial, angle_initial]
_move unpacks the action as ac, vc = action, so the first action value is the angle change and the second the velocity change
A step sets velocity to v + velocity_change*delta_T clipped to [velocity_min, velocity_max] and the angle to a + angle_change*delta_T clipped to [angle_change_min, angle_change_max]
A step then advances x by v_next*cos(angle_next)*delta_T + velocity_change*cos(angle_next)*delta_T**2/2 (sin for y) and clips each coordinate to [0, size]
reset sets timestep 0, previous_agent_location None, the agent at the starting location with risk from chance_constraint and the current gps_uncertainty, and the history to that one location
step increments timestep, adds gps_uncertainty_increment to gps_uncertainty, appends the new location to the history, and returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated=False and info
destination_tolerance is 1.5 m
is_done is true when the distance to the destination is below destination_tolerance or the agent failed
is_outofbounds is true when any coordinate is <= 0 or >= size
is_failed is true when the agent is out of bounds or its segment hits an obstacle
The reward is distance_weight*distance + steps_weight*len(agent_location_history) + risk_weight*risk, and math.inf when the agent failed
reward_weights defaults to distance 0.9, steps 0.1 and risk 0, and the constructor asserts that the weights sum to 1
A map JSON declares size in m, origin [x, y], destination [x, y] and a list of polygon obstacles
The 10x10_NoObstacle.json map has size 10, origin [1, 1], destination [9, 9] and no obstacles
step always returns truncated=False

determinism.notes: reset(seed) and cap.world.seed.v1 are accepted, but the environment draws no random numbers: a reset always starts at the map origin, so the same seed and actions reproduce the same trajectory.  The bridge reports seeded because the environment exposes no get_state/set_state for exact replay; the fake uses the same equations as the upstream class.

gaps: F0 kinematic point model: an action applies a velocity change and an angle change directly; there is no mass, force, drag, actuator, contact or friction model
no sensor or noise model: GPS uncertainty is a deterministic increment per step and risk is the obstacle chance constraint; the fake models the no-obstacle map, so its risk is always 0
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (delta_T 0.1 s) only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
the fake backend re-implements only the default 10x10 no-obstacle map, ignores map files, obstacles and the uav/reward configuration, and was not compared with the upstream environment

the upstream default map_filepath (itomori/navigation2d_config/maps/10x10/10x10_NoObstacle.json) does not match the data in the clone (itomori/envs/navigation2d_configs/maps/10x10/10x10_NoObstacle.json), so the sim backend needs an explicit map_filepath and was not run
the fake returns Python lists where upstream returns numpy arrays; both compute in float64 but the trigonometric calls and operation order differ, so state hashes can differ in the last bits
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
